3. The case of the plaintiffs in brief is that, one Abdus Subhan was the owner of the land described in the plot No. 15 including plot No. 16 and plot No. 14. The predecessor of the plaintiffs sheik Dengu alias Dengu Haji became the owner and possessor of the aforesaid land by way of purchase from Abdus Subhan. Gul Mamod, son of Abdus Subhan, died leaving his son Rashid Ullah and subsequently by amicable partition Lal Mamod and Lebus Ullah amicably partitioned the suit land whereby Lal Mamod got 11 Ana 8 Pai and Lebus Ullah got 5 Ana 4 Pai. By successive transfer the plaintiffs Nos. 1-4 got the suit land by way of purchase. In the survey and settlement operation the name of Lebus Ullah was correctly recorded but plot No. 14 and 16 was wrongly recorded in the name of the Government. In the above premise the predecessor of the plaintiff Nos. 1-10 and plaintiff Nos. 11-14 instituted Title Suit No. 132 of 1985 before the then Munsef, Baniyachong for declaration of title and obtained decree on 29.03.1986. The predecessor of the plaintiffs No. 1-10 instituted another Title Suit being No. 62 of 1987 for declaration of title and for injunction in respect of the land stated in 2nd schedule and obtained decree on 18.09.1988. Earlier the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 211 of 1961 for recovery of khas possession and after getting decree on 05.02.1966 got possession through execution case No. 75 of 1966. The plaintiffs on getting decree filed mutation Case No. 41 of 2001 to the office of the defendant No. 4 for the correction of record of right which was sent to defendant No.1 for final- approval but after elapse of long time no step was taken for disposal of the mutation case and as such the plaintiffs are constrained to file the suit seeking mandatory injunction. 

 4. Defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by filling written statement, denying the material allegation made in the plaint contending that plot No. 16 having area of 80 decimal and plot No. 14 having area of 10 decimal has rightly been recorded in the name of the Government and Government is in possession and control of the suit land. The defendants are not aware about the earlier decrees being, passed exparte and the Government is taking, preparation for initiating legal proceeding about those decrees. It has been further averred that a tender was floated to lease out the suit land, being pond in nature, and knowing fully well about the leasing process the plaintiff has filed the instant suit with a view to derive illegal gain and as such prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 7. Mr. Khair Ezaz Masood, along with Mr. Md. Shakhawat Hossain Khan, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that earlier the plaintiffs got decrees in their favour and got the possession therein by filing execution case. The judgment and decrees passed in favour of the plaintiffs has not been challenged at any point of time by the defendant and since no proceeding has been judgment initiated challenging the Judgment and decrees passed in favour of the plaintiffs, the decrees are valid in the eye of law which cannot be impugned or challenged in the instant proceeding. He next submits that section 54 of the State Acquisition and Tenency Act mandates that if a decree is passed by Civil Courts, the revenue authorities are obliged to correct record of right and make necessary alteration to give effect to the decree passed by the Civil Court. He next submits that as per section 54 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the opposite parties are obliged to give effect and correct record of right, but without taking effectual step, the matter has been kept pending for years together which constrainted the plaintiffs-petitioner to file the instant suit seeking mandatory injunction. He further submits that there is no bar in the Specific Relief Act for seeking mandatory injunction against the Government functionaries as they deliberately stalled order of Civil Court. He further submits that there is no bar in section 56 in passing mandatory injunction and there is no equally efficacious relief in other forum and hence the plaintiffs is constrained to initiate the instant proceeding. 

 9. Having gone through the pleadings, evidence and other material on record, it appears that the plaintiffs earlier of decrees their favour for declaration or title and recovery of khas possession and by filing execution case got delivery of possession. Although, the Government in the pleadings stated that they will take legal steps challenging those decrees but till date no step has been taken to this end. So, a decree whether exparte or contested has got sanctity until and unless such decrees are set aside, altered or varied. 

 10. It appears that the petitioners filed mutation case under section 54 of the State Acqusition and Tenency Act many years back and the assistant commissioner land referred the matter to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) for disposal but after elapse of many years no step has been taken for disposal of proceeding.

Regarding the question raised by learned Deputy Attorney General that the suit land being pond in type is non retainable land but the term pond does not strictly come within the preview of non retainable land as mandated in section 20(2)b and (2a) of the State Acquisition and tenancy Act. Any tank being excavated will not come within clutches of non retainable land. Conversely fishery being used for rearing and catching fish is non retainable and it is managed and controlled by the government.
